forgexSolutions.name: Revenue Leak Check
forgexSolutions.description: One-week audit ($500 fixed price, credited in full toward any fix ordered within 30 days) to measure how many calls, email-app form attempts, leads, and quotes slip through.

forgexSolutions.name: Lead-to-job pipeline
forgexSolutions.description: Captures every lead from web forms, email, and other sources into field-service software within two minutes, sends an instant reply, and tracks follow-up ($1,800 setup plus $149/month).
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential lead drop-off from the email-app contact form and manual follow-up delays during field work or outside business hours.

forgexSolutions.description: Answers routine homeowner questions using Walker Electric's existing 17 homeowner guides and service FAQs, collects project details/photos, and hands qualified estimate requests to the team (fixed price set after scoping).

feasibility.explanation: Replacing the client-side email-app form on https://walkerelectricidaho.com/contact/ with a server-side webhook and connecting incoming inquiries to an instant-reply and lead-tracking pipeline is technically straightforward. Furthermore, the site already has well-structured service FAQs and 17 homeowner articles on https://walkerelectricidaho.com/blog/ that could ground an AI support assistant if needed.

aiDelivery.explanation: Lead capture, routing, instant notifications, and follow-up reminders should be delivered through deterministic workflow automation for reliability. AI agents can assist by summarizing homeowner project descriptions, categorizing service types (Service Call, Lighting/Rewiring, Generator, Hot Tub, EV Charger, New Construction), and answering routine FAQ questions from the site's published guides before handing off to a licensed electrician.

humanReview: All electrical diagnostics, load calculations, code interpretations, and project estimates must be reviewed and approved by a licensed electrician before being sent to a customer.

Any AI support assistant must refrain from giving DIY electrical repair instructions or binding price quotes and immediately hand off troubleshooting or hazardous situations (such as buzzing panels, burning smells, or repeated breaker trips) to a human electrician.
Appointment scheduling that depends on location, permit coordination, or technician availability requires human confirmation.

risks.description: An AI assistant that provides inaccurate electrical advice or implies a fixed price before an on-site load calculation or diagnosis could create safety hazards or customer disputes.
Automated SMS or email replies to new leads must comply with TCPA consent requirements and CAN-SPAM regulations.
Homeowner contact details, home addresses, and project photos submitted during intake must be transmitted and stored securely with restricted access.

commercial.implementationCost: Revenue Leak Check: $500 fixed price (credited in full to any fix ordered within 30 days). Lead-to-job pipeline: $1,800 setup plus $149 per month. AI support assistant with human handoff: fixed price set after scoping.
assumptions: The website publishes no service prices or diagnostic call fees (stating only that estimates are free and pricing depends on project scope), so commercial value cannot be calculated from site prices.

discovery.outreachSubject: Question about the estimate form on walkerelectricidaho.com
discovery.outreachBody:
Hello Walker Electric LLC Leadership,

I was reviewing https://walkerelectricidaho.com/contact/ and noticed that your "Request a free estimate" form uses a "Prepare my request" button that opens the visitor's local email app rather than submitting directly on the page.

For electrical contractors, forms that rely on a visitor having an email app configured can sometimes cause homeowners—especially on mobile devices or outside your Monday–Friday 7:00 AM–5:00 PM hours—to drop off before their request reaches your inbox.

At ForgeX, we offer fixed-price automation services for home-service contractors, including a one-week Revenue Leak Check ($500 fixed price, credited in full toward any fix ordered within 30 days) and a Lead-to-job pipeline ($1,800 setup plus $149/month) that captures every web and email lead directly into your field-service software within two minutes and sends an instant reply.

If you already have a system handling this or if your current workflow is working well for your team size, no action is needed. If you would like to compare notes on how your web inquiries and follow-ups are currently routed, just reply to this email.

Best regards,

[FOUNDER_NAME]
[FOUNDER_TITLE], ForgeX
[FORGEX_POSTAL_ADDRESS]

If you prefer not to receive future emails from us, please reply with "unsubscribe" or use [OPT_OUT_MECHANISM].

limitations: Employee headcount is not stated on the website; the homepage uses singular phrasing ('One trusted electrician') while the Nampa page refers to 'Our licensed team', making it impossible to confirm from the website alone whether the company falls within ForgeX's target range of 10 to 75 staff.
Whether the company pays for leads cannot be confirmed from the public website (although googletagmanager.com is referenced in page metadata).

No individual is formally presented with an owner, executive, or manager title on the website outside of customer review text and an email address prefix, so no named individuals can be listed under verified decision-makers.
No specific Idaho electrical contractor license number or physical street address is published on the website.
No service prices or diagnostic fees are published on the website, preventing a supportable commercial value calculation.

qualification.rationale: Walker Electric LLC is a locally owned electrical contractor in the Treasure Valley of Idaho with a clear contact channel ([redacted]) and observable website friction (an estimate form on https://walkerelectricidaho.com/contact/ that opens the visitor's email app rather than capturing leads directly, plus no weekend hours or online booking). However, whether this causes actual lost revenue is a hypothesis rather than a confirmed customer problem, and the company's employee count (potentially smaller than ForgeX's 10–75 staff target given the homepage phrase 'One trusted electrician') and paid lead spend cannot be confirmed from the website alone. Accordingly, 'pursue later' after light discovery on team size and lead volume is the most accurate qualification.
